narrative:
The model estimated a 53.0% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In practical terms, that is a slightly-more-likely-than-not risk, not a certainty, but it crossed the threshold used for admission, so your application was denied.

The strongest reason was your part-time enrollment plan. Most accepted students study full-time (92.8%), and being part-time was the single largest factor pushing the prediction toward failure. Your first-year class standing was the next most influential factor: a decile of 8 is above the accepted-student average of 6, and it pushed toward passing. Your third-year standing was close to the accepted average and also pushed modestly toward passing, but it did not offset the part-time concern.

To improve your position, speak with admissions advising about whether full-time study is feasible and document any work or family obligations that require part-time status. Ask what evidence would reduce the predicted risk, such as a concrete full-time study plan, updated academic references, or a stronger recent academic record. Because the estimate is close to the threshold, a targeted explanation and plan may materially change the decision.
